common_name: Milkmaid Swamp Milkweed (White-Flowered Native Milkweed Selection)

planting.note: Direct sow or set out seed-grown transplants in spring into consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun; Milkmaid is a creamy white-flowered selection of swamp milkweed that otherwise keeps the wild species' upright habit and wetland tolerance.

directions: Milkmaid swaps the species' usual rose-pink umbels for clusters of fragrant, creamy white flowers held atop the same upright, clump-forming stems as wild swamp milkweed. Site it in consistently moist to wet, fertile soil in full sun, such as a rain garden, pond margin, or low spot that collects runoff, where it tolerates occasional standing water far better than most garden perennials. Like all swamp milkweed, it serves as a larval host for monarch caterpillars and a heavy nectar source for a wide range of butterflies, bees, and other pollinators through summer. Allow seed pods to mature and split for winter interest and self-sowing, or deadhead spent stalks to keep the clump tidier and limit volunteer seedlings.

planting.note: Plant after all danger of frost has passed; Rosea carries the same fine, twiggy texture as the species but opens its flowers in vivid fuchsia-pink instead of the typical lilac-purple.

directions: Rosea is a vivid pink-flowered selection of Mexican heather, covering its small, needle-like leaves in a nonstop scatter of tiny six-petaled fuchsia blooms from spring through frost. Grow it in well-drained soil in full sun for the densest flowering and tightest habit, though it tolerates light afternoon shade in the hottest Gulf Coast gardens. Its low, mounding form suits edging, mixed containers, and small-space groundcover use, where bees and small butterflies work the flowers all season. In zone 9, expect it to die back after a hard freeze and resprout readily from the base the following spring.

common_name: Lucky Star Dark Red Pentas (Compact Texas Superstar Star-Cluster Pentas)

planting.note: Transplant after soil has warmed following the last frost; Dark Red is the deepest, most saturated color in the dwarf Lucky Star seed series bred for Gulf South heat and humidity.

directions: Lucky Star Dark Red carries the deepest, most saturated flower color in the compact Lucky Star series, opening dense clusters of velvety red-black buds that mature to a rich true red. Its tight, uniform habit stays shorter and tidier than older pentas types, holding its shape in mass beds and containers through Gulf Coast summer heat without stretching or flopping. Grow in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil, watering regularly while plants establish; the dark color is especially effective as a hummingbird draw against lighter-colored series mates like Lavender or White. Light, steady feeding through the season keeps the compact clusters coming continuously from late spring to frost.

common_name: Lucky Star Lavender Pentas (Compact Texas Superstar Star-Cluster Pentas)

planting.note: Transplant after soil has warmed following the last frost; Lavender is the soft cool-toned color in the dwarf Lucky Star seed series bred for Gulf South heat and humidity.

directions: Lucky Star Lavender softens the compact Lucky Star series with cool, pale-violet flower clusters that read almost silvery from a distance, a gentle contrast to the Dark Red and Deep Pink selections in the same line. Plants hold the series' signature tight, dwarf habit, staying shorter and bushier than older pentas types even through the heaviest summer heat. Grow in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil and keep watering consistent while roots establish, then ease off once plants fill out. The pale blooms show especially well against darker foliage backdrops and draw a steady stream of butterflies and bees all summer into fall.

common_name: Starcluster Red Pentas (Vivid Red Egyptian Star Cluster)

planting.note: Set out transplants after all danger of frost has passed and soil has warmed, in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this vigorous bedding series stays compact and uniform, well suited to mass plantings and containers.

directions: Starcluster Red delivers the boldest, most saturated flower color in the Starcluster bedding series, with dense, rounded clusters of true-red, white-eyed florets that stand out even in intense summer glare. Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun and water regularly during establishment; once rooted in, it shrugs off Gulf Coast heat and humidity and draws hummingbirds reliably all season. The series' compact, uniform habit makes it dependable for mass color in beds and borders as well as large patio containers, holding its shape without staking. In zone 9b and warmer, established plants may survive a mild winter and resprout from the base.

common_name: Starcluster Lavender Pentas (Soft Lavender Egyptian Star Cluster)

planting.note: Set out transplants after all danger of frost has passed and soil has warmed, in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this vigorous bedding series stays compact and uniform, well suited to mass plantings and containers.

directions: Starcluster Lavender tones down the Starcluster series with soft lavender-pink florets around a small white eye, a gentler counterpoint to the series' bolder Red and Pink selections. Plants keep the same dense, rounded flower clusters and sturdy, uniform habit that make the Starcluster line reliable for mass bedding and large containers through hot, humid summers. Grow in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, watering consistently while plants establish and then as needed through the season. The muted color blends easily with other pastels in mixed beds while still drawing steady butterfly and bee activity.
